problem: Zero-shot object navigation methods rely on image-level VLM embeddings (CLIP, FLAVA) that lose object-level information, or on detectors (OWL-ViT) that are optimized for one image rather than retrieval over an image database. End-to-end RL approaches also only use within-episode experience and make failures hard to attribute.
motivation: Home robots need to find objects from free-form queries using memory of earlier exploration. Decoupling retrieval from navigation makes failures analyzable, but requires an image representation that scores well on multiple object queries per image, and stays stable under varied query phrasing.
key_idea: Fine-tune a VLM with a slot-attention object-centric image encoder and multi-label losses (Hungarian-matched box and contrastive losses), plus LLM-generated query augmentation and a noun+sentence prompt, to retrieve image-pose pairs from memory and navigate to them.
insight: Slot attention and multi-label training each hurt or barely help alone (AR@1 49.87 and 47.87 vs 50.88 baseline fine-tune), but together give 60.65, so slot attention needs local per-object supervision. The full loss set is also needed (contrastive only 46.62, box losses without MC loss 44.61 vs 60.65). The 'object noun + query sentence' prompt helps all VLMs, and LLM augmentation lifts AR@1 further (55.89 to 60.65 for the full prompt).
method: Object-centric image encoder: ViT-B/16 backbone plus slot-attention module (K=10 slots, U=20 iterations, GRU updates) whose slots decode to bounding boxes via MLPs; final embedding = MLP over concat of global feature and projected slots
Text encoder: BERT-tokenized text through a ViT-B/16-style transformer with linear projection (frozen during training); retrieval by dot-product similarity, top-k

Multi-label fine-tuning losses: CLIP-style contrastive loss on randomly permuted concatenated labels, Hungarian matching of slots to GT boxes, L1 + GIoU box losses, and multi-label contrastive loss between matched slots and label text embeddings (all weights 1)
LLM-based augmentation: GPT-3.5 noun-to-sentence and sentence-to-noun generation; converts SUN RGB-D detection labels into 10,670 multi-label caption queries
Prompt template: object noun followed by query text/sentence, used in both fine-tuning and inference
Navigation stack: SLAM-based mapping, global planner, local executor; robot goes to poses of top-k retrieved image-pose pairs and stops when the object is in view

setting.backbone: FLAVA-initialized ViT-B/16 image encoder + slot attention (fine-tuned); GPT-3.5 for query augmentation
setting.training_data: SUN RGB-D (5285 train images, 1067 object labels, 10,670 LLM-generated queries), fine-tuned 50k iterations; evaluated zero-shot on simulation and real data
setting.observation: RGB images with poses (image-pose memory from exploration); depth and stereo cameras for mapping
setting.action_space: Global plan to target pose via 'go to' command with waypoint-following local executor (non-holonomic ground robot)
setting.privileged: Exploration memory of image-pose pairs collected beforehand; no GT at test time for navigation

results: Retrieval: LOC-ZSON improves text-to-image AR@1 by 1.38-13.38% over the best baseline in most settings (60.65 vs ALIGN 53.88 in simulation). Navigation: it beats CoW (CLIP) at 2m goal success, 40 vs 27.5 in simulation and 66.67 vs 58.33 in the real world.
limitations: Representation only used for retrieval; no end-to-end RL or exploration integration, and depends on prior exploration memory
Small navigation evaluation (40 sim trials, 12 real trials), custom simulation, and SUN RGB-D evaluation labels are noisy (synonyms counted wrong)
Image-to-text retrieval is not consistently best (OWL-ViT-large is stronger in several settings)
